title: FairRARI: A Plug and Play Framework for Fairness-Aware PageRank
claim: Standard and post-processed fair rankings reach the fairness target by zeroing out many disadvantaged items; ours reaches it without such harm.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, same graph with node sizes encoding scores
description: Three side-by-side renderings of the same PolBooks political-books network. Red vertices form a dense cluster at the top and blue vertices form a cluster at the bottom, joined by a few purple-tinged edges. Vertex size encodes PageRank score. Panel (a), Original PR, shows large blue and red nodes of varied size, with red receiving only about 47% of the mass. Panel (b), Post-Processing, makes the red nodes large and shrinks many blue nodes to empty black-outlined circles, meaning zero score. Panel (c), FairRARI, keeps the red nodes large and leaves every blue node as a small but filled dot. Captions below each panel read (a) Original PR, (b) Post-Processing, (c) FairRARI. The eye goes first to the black hollow circles in the middle panel.
caption: Standard PageRank (PR) and fair PR vectors under $\phi$-fairness [ref] with two vertex groups (red/blue) on the PolBooks dataset. Vertex size is proportional to the PR score produced by each method. Black circles indicate vertices with zero PR score. The standard PR vector (a) assigns $\phi^red_\mathrm{o}\! =\! 0.47$ of the total PR mass to the red group. The target for the fair PR vectors is $\phi^red\! =\! 0.9$ of total mass for the red group. While both fair PR vectors in (b) and (c) attain this target, $37/49 \approx 75%$ of blue vertices in (b) are set to zero, while $0%$ of the blue vertices suffer such an undesirable outcome for FairRARI (c).
abstract: PageRank (PR) is a fundamental algorithm in graph machine learning tasks. Owing to the increasing importance of algorithmic fairness, we consider the problem of computing PR vectors subject to various group-fairness criteria based on sensitive attributes of the vertices. At present, principled algorithms for this problem are lacking - some cannot guarantee that a target fairness level is achieved, while others do not feature optimality guarantees. In order to overcome these shortcomings, we put forth a unified in-processing convex optimization framework, termed FairRARI, for tackling different group-fairness criteria in a ``plug and play'' fashion. Leveraging a variational formulation of PR, the framework computes fair PR vectors by solving a strongly convex optimization problem with fairness constraints, thereby ensuring that a target fairness level is achieved. We further introduce three different fairness criteria which can be efficiently tackled using FairRARI to compute fair PR vectors with the same asymptotic time-complexity as the original PR algorithm. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets showcase that FairRARI outperforms existing methods in terms of utility, while achieving the desired fairness levels across multiple vertex groups; thereby highlighting its effectiveness.
